basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; visual accommodation dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Microtia alone does not establish hearing loss or functional ear damage.

decisions.otologic: none: microtia occurs in 80-99%, but external-ear dysmorphism alone does not establish functional damage; hearing impairment is not documented.

basis: Skin fragility and defining enamel hypoplasia; oral mucosal blistering occurs in 80-99%. Anemia is secondary to wounds, inflammation or nutritional loss, without direct blood-cell disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia is frequent (30-79%) but secondary to wounds, inflammation or nutritional loss; direct hematologic injury is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: enamel hypoplasia is explicitly part of the disease definition; oral mucosal blistering also affects 80-99%.

basis: Larval Taenia tissue infection; CNS cysts directly injure neural tissue in roughly half of reported human cases. Ocular and subcutaneous sites are less frequent.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS coenuri cause direct neural injury in roughly half of reported human cases, exceeding the approximate 30% threshold.

basis: Reduced spinal cord perfusion defines the condition; the affected tissue is neural. Associated arterial or aortic disease is an underlying cause, not a required manifestation.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: spinal cord ischemia does not require intrinsic vessel disease; arterial/aortic disorders are possible causes rather than damage caused by this condition.

basis: Autoimmune sterile endocardial/valvular vegetations define disease. Embolic cerebrovascular disease is a separately diagnosed complication, despite being described as common.

decisions.neurologic: none: embolic cerebrovascular disease is a separately diagnosed complication; the definition's description as common does not override the separate-disease exclusion.

basis: Ethmoid sinus mucosal inflammation is an upper-airway disorder. The umbrella definition establishes neither a specific infection nor an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: nonspecific sinus mucosal inflammation alone does not establish infection or an autoimmune/immune-mediated disease across this acute/chronic umbrella.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and characteristic intestinal aganglionosis define syndrome; congenital heart defects occur in ~50-60%. Incontinence alone does not establish urinary tract damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: the synonym explicitly defines Hirschsprung disease with intellectual disability; aganglionic megacolon is a characteristic structural lesion (30-79%).

basis: Pituitary/CNS malformations; hearing loss and night blindness each 80-99%. Spine/joint and oral malformations (80-99%) omitted at cap; sensory findings document functional loss.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft palate/oral defects (80-99%) qualify, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of documented hearing and visual loss.
decisions.ocular: involved: non-progressive night blindness is direct visual dysfunction, annotated in 80-99%; retained under the cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: spinal, scoliosis and joint defects (80-99%) qualify, but are omitted at the four-axis cap; hearing and visual loss establish functional damage.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment is direct ear functional loss, annotated in 80-99%; retained under the cap.

basis: Mirror positioning of heart, liver and gut defines condition; pulmonary situs omitted at the three-primary cap. Reversal alone does not establish functional organ damage.

decisions.hepatic: primary: mirror positioning of the liver is a defining abdominal anatomical feature of complete situs inversus.
decisions.pulmonary: none: reversed pulmonary situs is omitted under the three-primary cap; position alone does not establish lung damage warranting involved.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy and myopathy each 80-99%. Renal tubulopathy, optic neuropathy and hearing loss also 80-99%, omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy/leukodystrophy occur in 80-99%; neural injury is a manifestation of the metabolic defect, not required across all complex I deficiency subtypes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: mitochondrial myopathy occurs in 80-99%; muscle injury is a common manifestation rather than the defining biochemical defect of this heterogeneous umbrella.
